messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: ADMIN: Re: IMPRESIONANTE
parts:
Dear distance-sampling list members,

You will no doubt be aware of the recent postings by Sr. Aguillar, the first
of which contained some large image files as attachments. None of the
messages were appropriate for the distance-sampling list, and I suspect they
were posted partly because of Sr. Aguillar's ignorance of standard netiquette
and partly because he didn't read the list guidelines (available at
http://www.mailbase.ac.uk/lists/distance-sampling/ as file Introduction, and
posted to all new list members).

The distance-sampling list is not moderated: any member of the list can post
what they wish. This leaves us open to inappropriate postings, either from
ill-informed or malicious people. I would rather not have to moderate the
list, due to the increased administrative burden. Fortunately we have not
been plagued by inappropriate postings much to date. However, if such
incidents become more common then I will have to switch the list to a
moderated one. Meanwhile, I hope that this one incident does not put you off
remaining a member of what is usually thought of as a low-volume, high
quality list.

As an aside, I congratulate all members of the list for not making the
mistake of posting any response to Sr. Aguillar's message on the list. As
you no doubt know, if you see a message on an email list that appears
inappropriate the best course of action is usually to ignore it: the list
owner will no doubt be contacting the originator. If you feel you must
respond, send a message to the person who posted the message and copy it to
the list owner.

If you have any comments or suggestions about this message, feel free to
contact me.

- Len Thomas
distance-sampling list admin
distance-sam...@mailbase.ac.uk

--
Len Thomas (l...@mcs.st-and.ac.uk)
Research Unit for Wildlife Population Assessment
Mathematical Institute, University of St Andrews
Scotland
